text.p: **BIRTHDAYS**
Australian pioneer GEORGE ANGAS was born in England in 1789. He brought a large group of German Lutherans with him to South Australia, who began the wine industry in the Barossa Valley.
Canadian-born American actor GLENN FORD was born in 1916. His best known film was "Blackboard Jungle".
Labor politician LANCE BARNARD was born in Launceston in 1919. He began his career as a teacher, and became a politician in 1954. He became Deputy Prime Minister under GOUGH WHITLAM.
American author JOSEPH HELLER who wrote "Catch 22" was born in 1923.
Australian actor JOHN MEILLON was born in 1934. He appeared in films like "Crocodile Dundee", and "The Sundowners", but has been best remembered for his appearance in "The Fourth Wish".
American singer and pianist RITA COOLIDGE was born in 1945.
**EVENTS**
1707 : Scotland and England were joined together under
the name of Great Britain.
1851 : Queen VICTORIA opened the famous Crystal Palace in
London.
1873 : Explorer DAVID LIVINGSTONE died of malaria at

Chitambo in the middle of Africa. LIVINGSTONE went missing for some years while searching for the source of the Nile. That was until journalist HENRY STANLEY found him and greeted him with the famous words "Dr LIVINGSTONE I presume."
1876 : The Royal Titles Bill was passed by the British
parliament, entitling Queen VICTORIA to call herself Empress of India.
1898 : In the Battle of Manila Bay in the
Spanish-American War, U.S. forces destroyed the Spanish fleet and blockaded the bay for three months before capturing Manila itself.
1915 : The liner Lusitania left New York on the same day

the German Embassy took out advertisements warning anyone travelling on ships carrying a British flag that they did so at their own risk. It was sunk six days later. The sinking ultimately resulted in the U.S. entering World War I.
1931 : The Empire State Building was opened in New York.
1941 : ORSON WELLES' film "Citizen Kane" opened in New
York. The film is considered one of the greatest ever made.
1945 : Hamburg radio officially announced that HITLER had
died in Berlin; Nazi leader JOSEPH GOEBBELS commited suicide in his Berlin bunker; German HQ in Italy formally agreed to an unconditional surrender.
1960 : American pilot GARY POWERS was captured by the
Russians after his U2 spy plane was shot down over the Soviet Union.
1961 : Cuban leader FIDEL CASTRO declared the country a
socialist nation and abolished elections.
1967 : ELVIS PRESLEY married PRISCILLA BEAULIEU.
1989 : A large anti-government protest in Czechoslovakia
demanded the release of playwright VACLAV HAVEL.
1991 : CHRIS PATTEN was elevated to the British cabinet,
and remarked, "In a democracy, everybody has the right to be represented, including the jerks."
1992 : Turkmenistan announced it would switch to a
Latin-based Turkish alphabet from the Cyrillic script.
1993 : Sri Lankan President RANASINGHE PREMADASA died of
injuries sustained in a bomb blast during a May Day procession.
1994 : AYRTON SENNA, three times world F-1 auto racing
champion, died after a high-speed crash in the San Marino Grand Prix.
1994 : Wigan won the rugby league Challenge Cup in
Britain, defeating Leeds 26-16.
1995 : Croatia recaptured the rebel Serb enclave of
Western Slavonia it lost in 1991.
